houses.name: Apollo / Torsten Sløk
houses.title: Warsh Lets the Rate Hike Do the Talking
houses.vsClause: They did not read Liquidity, Rates, Growth, Inflation, or Risk.
houses.quote: Fed press conferences began in 2011, and the chart below plots the total number of questio
quotes: Fed press conferences began in 2011, and the chart below plots the total number of questions asked against the median words per answer for every one of them.

At his June and July press conferences, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh followed the same pattern as previous Fed chairs, but in September, he took fewer questions and gave shorter, more focused answers, letting the rate hike speak more for itself.

houses.name: UBS CIO
houses.title: How will Fed rate hikes impact markets?
houses.assets: Equities IN; fixed income Attractive, including medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds; cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit
houses.vsClause: Rates matches (Leaning tight). Growth matches (Leaning strong). Their Inflation is Mid; ours is Leaning hot. Risk matches (Risk-on). They stay with equities, which are out.
houses.quote: equities withstand such a shallow tightening cycle
quotes: But we expect only one further rate increase and believe resilient growth and robust earnings should help equities withstand such a shallow tightening cycle.
Investors should maintain diversified equity exposure and use the rise in yields to add selectively to quality bonds, while remaining cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit.
